newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks dip, market to recover.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks dip, market to recover.

text.p: Most Croatian stocks dipped on Friday, ending the week lower amid very weak buying interest but traders predicted a market recovery with possible small price fluctuations next week.
"Small investors are in a panic to sell, they have knocked down some prices," said Zoran Ilic of Consult Invest brokerage.
He said the reason for that might be "psychological" as local shareholders were nervous of possible effects the voucher privatisation scheme may have on their investments.
The authorities last week published a list of assets in over 800 companies to be distributed among refugees and war victims in exchange for vouchers.
But exceptionally low prices of some stocks may now be a signal to other investors to buy again, Ilic said.
Nine of 15 active issues fell on Friday, four rose and two were flat. Volume was slightly lower at 10,704 shares and turnover also fell to five from 7.8 million kuna.
Most actively traded, drugs firm Pliva, inched up four kuna to 425 on volume of 5,342 shares. Traders expected the stock to remain stable next week, if not rise.
Another fully-listed issue, Zagrebacka Banka, inched down five kuna to 1,820 on volume of 319 shares.

Ilic expected a period of stability for bank stocks, with only a possible price correction for Varazdinska Banka. Its first issue was not traded on Friday but someone paid 42,000 kuna for it in a deal with a single share a day earlier.

Food processor Podravka edged down nine kuna to 301, with 2,077 units sold. Confectioner Kras lost 11 kuna to 450. But traders said lower prices of both stocks were only temporary and expected them to recover shortly.
Biggest loser -- electrical group Koncar Elektroindustrija -- tumbled 245 kuna to 905, but only 21 shares were sold.
Top gainer was hotelier Zlatni rat from the Dalmatian island of Brac, adding 40 kuna to 150 and selling 55 units in a first deal since last October.
Other hotel stocks were among decliners, with only Suncani Hvar remaining flat at 66 kuna. Traders described their low prices as "surprising".
